findings.summary: SC-3 (delivered by this job per plan.json) asks for a CI step that installs a checksum-verified, pinned gitleaks and runs `gitleaks git` over full history against `.gitleaksignore`. Nothing in this diff or already on main exercises any of that: there is no test or check script anywhere in the tree that simulates a checksum mismatch and asserts the install step fails, that lints/parses .github/workflows/ci.yml, or that runs `gitleaks git . --config .gitleaks.toml --gitleaks-ignore-path .gitleaksignore` and asserts it comes back clean (grep for 'gitleaksignore', 'GITLEAKS_SHA256', and 'ci.yml' outside docs/work/secret-scan and this diff's own two files found nothing). The job's own 'verified' record (journal.jsonl line 29 / built-3-1.json) reports the standard per-package checks (typecheck/lint/tests per unit, duplication(.)) — none of which read .github/workflows/ci.yml or .gitleaksignore at all, since neither file is source for any of those units. 'verified: true' for this job therefore proves the diff didn't break an existing package; it proves nothing about SC-3's own behavior. One concrete illustration of what that gap leaves unchecked: work-order.json (line 4) catalogues 'fake_api_key' in daemon/tests/integration/test_context_assistant.py as one of the 6 historical generic-api-key findings the full-history scan must not choke on, but that name appears nowhere in .gitleaks.toml's allowlist comments (which name only the current variable, 'fake_llm_service_key' — confirmed by reading the file at daemon/tests/integration/test_context_assistant.py:338, and by grepping docs/work/no-internal-mocks/job-1.diff, which also shows only 'fake_llm_service_key') nor in this job's .gitleaksignore (one entry, covering only test_analyzer_integration.py). If the historical 'fake_api_key' commit held a literal different from the two values .gitleaks.toml's allowlist already anchors on, CI's full-history step would surface it as an un-ignored 17th finding and fail the job on a known fake rather than a real one — the opposite of what SC-3 asks. This review has no git-history access (no shell/log tool) to confirm the literal one way or the other, so this is raised as an unverified risk under the broader coverage gap, not a confirmed defect.
